workbench:
Use case: premium website art direction / desktop section mockup. Create ONE exceptionally polished, believable screenshot of a redesigned Sonar social-listening website audience section. It must feel custom-designed at the level of a leading independent design studio: editorial typography, tactile photographic art direction, intentional asymmetry, and exceptionally clear product relevance. Not a SaaS template, not a generic three-card grid, not a dashboard. Show real website scale and surrounding warm ivory whitespace. Landscape canvas around 1600x1100.

ART DIRECTION: "THE WORKBENCH". One continuous, beautifully photographed creative worktable, viewed directly from above, becomes a stage for three kinds of marketing work. The interface selects one role at a time. Show the BRAND MARKETERS state selected. Warm ivory #f8f7ef, ink-teal #12383c, muted sea-glass #e4efea, ONE coral #ee7863 accent. Real photographic objects and real warm-brown feminine hands with natural nails; no men, no large portraits, no people posing, no rendered plastic, no sci-fi. Strict art-directed restraint.

LAYOUT:
At the very top a slim real page nav: small bold sans-serif "sonar." left; Product / Niches / Pricing / Sign in and a modest "Get a free report" pill right.
Below, plenty of whitespace. Small upper-case eyebrow "YOUR ROLE. YOUR NEXT MOVE."
A confident left-aligned heading spanning about 70% width in superbly kerned bold grotesk, approximately 68px actual website size:
"Built around the person
doing the work."
Only "doing the work." has a fine coral underline, hand-drawn but very controlled.
Beside heading on right, a small beautifully typeset supporting sentence: "Different desks. Different decisions. The same clear view of your market."

Below this header: a large borderless rectangular photographic stage taking LEFT 65% of the content width; rounded corners only 16px, not a bubbly panel. RIGHT 30% is a meticulous editorial role selector and role-specific copy. The photo should be about 690px wide and 470px high at realistic web scale. Give the whole section generous breathing room. No giant full-screen face.

PHOTOGRAPH:
An extraordinary overhead photograph of a pale sea-glass matte desk, with strong yet soft afternoon window light and tangible microtextures. A silver laptop enters cropped from the UPPER LEFT edge at a deliberate diagonal, its visible screen displaying a clean simple social-content research view with three realistic miniature female creator video thumbnails (skin-care bottle demo, fitness routine, coffee product demo), no charts, no fabricated numbers. From lower left, one real female hand rests naturally on the trackpad, doing actual work. At upper middle/right, an ivory compact digital camera lies beside a short deep-teal woven strap with tiny coral stitch. At lower middle a slender black phone lies at a slight angle, showing a female creator demonstrating an ivory skincare bottle. A real female right hand reaches from the RIGHT edge and gently rotates the phone to inspect the clip. Keep all anatomy natural. Add one small unbranded cream skincare product standing near the phone as a link between the content and the physical brand. Small espresso glass at far top right, genuine material reflection, soft contact shadows. These few objects are meticulously balanced, casually precise, and photographically real. NO paper, notebooks, boards, busy scatter or fake floating UI. A fine coral line may run along the desk's left edge as a brand accent but not across objects. This is an actual workbench seen in a high-end editorial still-life, rich enough to animate subtly later.

RIGHT UI:
Three stacked role rows with hairline separators, large deliberate spacing:
"01  Brand marketers  ↗" ACTIVE, dark teal type and a coral small square.
"02  Agencies" muted
"03  Founders" muted
The active row expands into editorial copy:
"You own the plan.
Know the whole field."
Then a short, readable description:
"See the competitors, creators and content shaping your category."
Three tiny neat text links separated by dots:
"Competitor activity · Creator discovery · Better briefs"
Below a plain ink-teal underlined action "See your market →".
The other two roles are collapsed quiet rows, not rounded cards. Use good accessible readable text sizes.

Under the photo, on ivory, a small caption left "01 / A CLEARER BRIEF STARTS HERE" and right "Brand marketers". At the bottom a delicate fine rule, tiny text "Brand marketers / Agencies / Founders", and next section whitespace. No invented logos, client names, testimonials, metrics or outcome claims. No stars, shiny gradients, giant decorative numbers, stock photos, neon, holograms, sonic rings. The result should look tactile, confident, sophisticated and real. Carefully typeset text must be legible and exactly spelled. This is a fully designed section concept, not a moodboard.
campaignRoom:
Use case: premium website art direction / desktop section mockup. Create ONE extraordinarily polished alternative design for Sonar's "Built around the person doing the work" website section. Theme: "THE CAMPAIGN ROOM". Make the section feel like a cinematic editorial story with an immersive photographic environment and incredibly refined typography. This must be a fresh alternative to a three-card grid and to a tabletop flat lay. It must communicate Brand marketers, Agencies, and Founders clearly. Show a plausible real website screenshot at desktop scale, landscape 1600x1100. No men, no oversized face, no mannequin, no anime, no shiny AI render. All photography is photoreal, visibly tactile, editorial. No fake metrics, invented customers or claims.

PAGE DESIGN:
Warm ivory background #f8f7ef, ink teal #12383c typography, pale sea-glass details, subtle coral as the sole accent.
Top slim navbar with "sonar." in small bold clean sans serif on left, Product / Niches / Pricing / Sign in and a modest "Get a free report" button right.
Below 60px whitespace, a small widely tracked "WHO IT'S FOR" eyebrow. Set the exact headline "Built around the person doing the work." in two exquisite bold grotesk lines, approx 62px website size, left aligned, with beautifully measured whitespace and a short fine coral underline. A tiny supporting sentence sits far right: "See your market. Make your move."

MAIN SECTION:
One large cinematic panoramic photograph, almost full width, about 1350x580px in the represented website, with restrained 18px corners. It is not divided into cards. The upper 75% of the photo shows an authentic bright creative studio from a beautiful slightly elevated diagonal camera angle with a 50mm photographic feel. Center-left: an ADULT FEMALE creative strategist in an oversized white shirt with casually rolled sleeves, dark hair in a loose bun, seen in PROFILE FROM BEHIND so face is tiny and incidental, seated on a sculptural dark wood chair at a long low pale oak worktable. She is actively reviewing a social video on a large thin widescreen monitor; her right hand is on a trackpad, gaze fixed on the monitor. Monitor shows three real portrait video thumbnails of female skincare, fitness, and lifestyle creators, with one restrained dark teal interface column. No charts, number metrics or massive unreadable text blocks. One slim phone leans on a stand beside the monitor showing a product video, and a tiny ivory product bottle ties it to a real client brief. The person occupies less than 18% of the entire photograph, not a portrait.

To the RIGHT of the photograph, a genuine small filming setup is visible: a single slender camera tripod aimed at a cream product on an understated sea-glass plinth near a huge soft window. One folded coral backdrop fabric on a small stool gives warmth. Background has large soft ivory plaster curves, actual window shadows and pale sage curtains moving almost imperceptibly, with a tiny view of cloudy sky. The space is architectural and calm, not a corporate office or stock-photo coworking room. Uncluttered. Every object has a purpose in making and assessing marketing content. This scene should feel like the opening frame of a beautifully photographed brand film.

INTEGRATED INTERFACE:
Along the BOTTOM 25% of the photograph place a perfectly designed OPAQUE deep-ink-teal editorial strip, flush with image edges, not floating translucent glass cards.
Divide the strip by two very fine vertical rules into three role selectors, but maintain one uninterrupted strip. Left is ACTIVE:
"01  Brand marketers" in ivory, coral 22px line over it; below "Own the next move." in refined 24px grotesk, and tiny "See your market →".
Middle: "02  Agencies" in muted sage, then "Bring the evidence." in smaller subdued type.
Right: "03  Founders" in muted sage, then "Find your opening." in smaller subdued type.
A very fine coral progress line runs just above the strip under the active first third, indicating an optional quiet scene transition. Do NOT show a video-player timeline, speaker, fake analytics, extra labels or a play icon.
Below photograph on ivory, a short line of copy aligned left:
"From the first question to the next brief, work with a clear view of your category."
Aligned right three small scope words: "Competitors / Creators / Content".

No glassmorphism, blob shapes, skeuomorphic folders, scattered card stacks, large floating faces, generic agency headshots, thumbs-up, awards or fictitious testimonials. The emotional feel is cinematic creative confidence, human craft and decisive marketing work. Beautiful photograph; sophisticated section hierarchy; restrained elegant UI. It should look like a real fully finished award-caliber product marketing website concept, not a poster or moodboard.
